requirements.title: Entrance to major
requirements.summary: Entrance requires GPA 2.6 through the request semester and C or better in the source-listed entry courses. Entry conditions do not create additional course identities: Entrance to Major In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: Have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better in each prior to enrolling in the degree program: MATH 140 , MATH 141 , ( CMPSC 131 or CMPSC 121 ) , ( CMPSC 132 or CMPSC 122 ), PHYS 211 . Have achieved a minimum grade point average of 2.6 prior to and through the end of the semester during which the entrance to major is requested.

requirements.title: General Education distribution
requirements.summary: 45 semester hours: GQ 6 and GWS 9 with C or better; breadth GA, GHW, GH, GS and GN 3 each; Inter-Domain 6; exploration GN 3 plus eligible domains 6. Foundations/breadth exclude Inter-Domain. Exploration permits the stated advanced-world-language condition. Major overlap is limited to the program-specific allocation.

requirements.title: Cultures and writing overlays
requirements.summary: US cultures 3 plus international cultures 3 may satisfy other requirements. Three writing-across-curriculum credits must come from the college of graduation; no extra course count is inferred from overlays.

requirements.title: University completion and credit-source conditions
requirements.summary: Complete the major and earn at least 2.00 GPA within the degree program. University minimum is 120 credits, overridden by a higher program minimum. The dean/chancellor and faculty may require up to 24 major credits at the degree location/program; source/time restrictions remain subject to Senate 83-80. First-year engagement depends on the college plan.

requirements.title: Engineering major and GE accounting
requirements.summary: Major 102–103 semester hours; 21 GE hours overlap (GN 6, GQ 6, GWS 9). The remaining 24 GE hours must be distinct from the major. The degree minimum is 126, not the sum of all option identities. C-minimum designations are scoped to the table sections that explicitly require them.

requirements.title: Credit unit definition
requirements.summary: Penn State courses carry semester hours of credit; the institution evaluates conversion from other credit systems. This is an explicit unit definition, not an inference from the academic calendar.

requirements.title: Local-residence requirement disclosure
requirements.summary: A college/campus/program may require up to 24 major credits locally. Specific courses cannot be mandated except a required senior seminar or capstone. Such requirements must appear in the academic plan, Bulletin major description and college/department graduation materials; advising must address them. Students can raise noncompliance with the undergraduate associate dean.

requirements.title: Transfer review and graduation-document deadline
requirements.summary: Before taking outside courses, use the transfer-credit tool and consult an adviser about transferability and degree applicability. Unevaluated courses require a current syllabus and formal review. Official credit documents must reach Admissions at least 30 days before the graduating semester’s last class day; college approval is required for deadline exceptions.

requirements.title: General education distribution, breadth and overlap
requirements.summary: The 45-credit GE allocation is 15 foundations (9 writing/speaking, 6 quantification), 15 breadth (3 in each of five domains), 6 integrative studies and 9 exploration. Foundations require C and cannot be inter-domain; breadth also excludes inter-domain. Exploration requires 3 natural-science credits plus 6 from permitted domains, including limited advanced language. Breadth/exploration cannot use the major’s own department/program or its cross-listed courses; integrative studies is exempt. Published flexibility permits appropriate 200–499 substitutions and qualifying language beyond degree minima. Program-identified major overlap is limited by the domain caps; integrative-study courses cannot enter that overlap statement.

requirements.title: Department supporting-list boundary
requirements.summary: The department confirms 27 approved technical-elective credits, including 15 at the 400 level, plus 3 approved nontechnical credits and a one-credit seminar. This public page does not enumerate or link the approved lists. Its condensed additional-course presentation is not used to replace the Bulletin’s separate programming sequences and speech alternatives.

requirements.title: Conditional Schreyer communication route
requirements.summary: Incoming Schreyer Honors College first-year students at University Park take ENGL 137H/CAS 137H in fall and ENGL 138T/CAS 138T in spring, three credits each. Where the program prescribes GWS courses, this sequence replaces the listed first-year composition and speech requirements. Slash-linked listings are source labels; this note does not independently certify cross-list identity or add universal fixed courses.

requirements.title: Published residence rules and pending revision notice
requirements.summary: The currently displayed Senate 83-80 text requires 36 of the final 60 baccalaureate credits in university/cooperative programs, and the final 60 credits for a first bachelor degree within five calendar years, extended for intervening military service. Stricter college rules and dean-level appeals remain possible. The page labels June 23, 2026 revisions pending implementation. This dated inventory retains the displayed rules and notice; it does not apply an unverified future replacement or infer its effective cohort.

requirements.title: Catalog cohort and program-change resolution
requirements.summary: University and program requirements are those in effect at the first scheduled class meeting after the most recent degree-candidate admission. Approved later changes must be communicated by the program head. Students should seek resolution with the program; when agreement is not reached, the relevant dean may approve an equitable program of study.

requirements.title: University GPA and degree-exception authority
requirements.summary: The displayed Senate 82-40 rule requires at least a 2.00 average in Penn State coursework; designated C-required major courses must separately meet that grade. The page marks March 31, 2026 GPA revisions and June 23, 2026 exception-policy revisions pending implementation. Under the displayed 82-60 text, deans may approve college/university exceptions within policy intent, program chairs may approve major exceptions subject to dean review, and extraordinary requests go to the Senate academic-standards subcommittee. Approved exceptions must be recorded; none is presumed granted.

requirements.title: EECS substitutions and prerequisite procedures
requirements.summary: The common EECS advising FAQ directs substitutions to the university review system and requires entrance-to-major petitions before the major request. Prerequisites are enforced; a pending substitution, summer course or outside course may require a separate prerequisite override request. Approval is conditional. The FAQ excludes STAT 480/481/482/483 from degree use. Its AIE handbook link returns to the public AI engineering degree page rather than supplying the referenced approved elective lists. Rules explicitly naming other majors are not silently extended to AIE.

notes: The current major, named options, college and university policies have been reviewed within the recorded source scope. Remaining exact source gaps are listed in the curriculum audit; the record does not certify a complete degree inventory.

The atlas records the Senate rules currently displayed with their pending-implementation notices. It does not apply unverified revised rules or claim they are already effective. Prerequisite-only preparation is not added to fixed degree counts.
